result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers name the specific Polish, Turkish and Vietnamese characters to check, explain that missing glyphs fall back to another font, and warn that tall stacked marks can collide or be clipped. B is slightly better: it gives a concrete fallback font stack, ties the font choice to each kind of text, and says plainly that the font's coverage and licence can't be judged without seeing the font. A has a handy single test string and useful notes on subsetting and storing names in precomposed form, but it is less explicit about what it can't verify. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover coverage, fallback, licensing, line-height and lang/casing well. B is more concrete: it lists the needed characters for each language with Unicode block names, gives a ready-made test string, and adds the practical delivery points of unicode-range subsetting and NFC normalisation. A is more open about what can't be checked without seeing the font, but it is a bit less specific in its testing guidance.
